name: Tanchiawn
ingredients: 500g pork belly, cut into 2-inch chunks (with skin for depth)
200g fermented bamboo shoot (tuai), rinsed and chopped (homemade preferred)
1 cup water (or bamboo tube water for extra flavor)
instructions: 1. Heat mustard oil in a heavy pan until smoking. Add dried red chilies and garlic; sizzle for 20 seconds.
2. Add sliced onions and ginger; sauté until onions are translucent and golden.
3. Add pork pieces; sear on all sides until browned, about 5 minutes.
4. Stir in turmeric powder and salt; cook for 1 minute.
5. Add chopped fermented bamboo shoot and green chilies; mix well.
6. Pour in water; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45-60 minutes until pork is tender and flavors meld.
7. Adjust salt and garnish with fresh coriander. Serve with steamed rice.
description: A smoky, heart-warming embrace of fermented bamboo and mountain herbs, simmered with pork in a garlicky broth.
